saints.name: Pope St. Anicetus
saints.title: Pope and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: An early pope who received St. Polycarp and kept charity amid the dispute over Easter…
biography: A Syrian from Emesa, the modern Homs, Anicetus governed the Roman church in the middle of the second century, from about 157 to 168, when Gnostic teachers such as Valentinus and Marcion were troubling it; against them he held fast to the apostolic faith. The Liber Pontificalis recalls even his ruling that the clergy must not wear long hair.

His pontificate is lit by the visit, about 155, of the aged Polycarp of Smyrna, disciple of the Apostle John. They could not agree about Easter — the churches of Asia kept it on the fourteenth of Nisan with the Passover, Rome on the Sunday — yet neither broke communion: Anicetus in deference let Polycarp celebrate the Eucharist in his own church, and they parted in peace.

The traveler Hegesippus also visited Rome in his days, a sign of the see's early eminence. Anicetus died in April about the year 168 and was buried, the Liber Pontificalis says, in the cemetery of Callixtus on the Appian Way; later tradition counts him among the martyrs, though his martyrdom is not historically attested.
saints.knownFor: His charity toward St. Polycarp in the early Easter controversy.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain), 17 April
